record.paper_title: Open Problems in Partial Differential Equations Arising from Fluid Dynamics
record.original_question: For renormalized weak solutions of the general nonlinear Boltzmann equation in the sense of DiPerna-Lions, what regularity can be proved, and can one then rigorously derive their hydrodynamic limit toward macroscopic fluid equations?

evidence.quote: Other related questions, such as ... the regularity of the renormalized weak solutions to Boltzmann equations due to Diperna-Lions ([77]) and its hydro-dynamic limit, are waiting to be attacked too.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the nonlinear Boltzmann equation
  ∂_t f + v · ∇_x f = Q(f, f),    (t,x,v) ∈ (0,∞) × ℝ^d_x × ℝ^d_v,
where Q(f,f) is the standard Boltzmann collision operator
  Q(f,f)(v) = ∫_{ℝ^d} ∫_{S^{d-1}} B(v−v_*, σ) [ f(v')f(v'_*) − f(v)f(v_*) ] dσ dv_*,
with pre/post-collisional velocities v' = (v+v_*)/2 + |v−v_*|σ/2, v'_* = (v+v_*)/2 − |v−v_*|σ/2 and a physical collision kernel B ≥ 0.

A nonnegative function f ∈ C([0,∞); L^1_{loc}(ℝ^d_x × ℝ^d_v)) is a renormalized weak solution in the DiPerna–Lions sense if for every β ∈ C^1([0,∞)) with β'(s)(1+s) bounded one has, in the sense of distributions,
  ∂_t β(f) + v · ∇_x β(f) = β'(f) Q(f,f),
with finite mass, energy and entropy initially, and Q(f,f)/(1+f) ∈ L^1_{loc}.

(a) Establish a quantitative regularity theory for such renormalized weak solutions: identify a functional space (e.g. Sobolev, Besov, or fractional regularity in x and/or v) in which an arbitrary global renormalized solution must lie, given only finite mass, energy and entropy of the initial datum, for a general physically admissible collision kernel B (both cutoff and non-cutoff cases).

(b) Using such regularity, give a rigorous derivation of the hydrodynamic limit: prove that, under the appropriate diffusive (or other) scaling f_ε of renormalized solutions with mean free path ε → 0, the suitably rescaled fluctuations of f_ε converge to a weak solution of the corresponding macroscopic fluid system (incompressible Navier–Stokes–Fourier, incompressible Euler, or compressible Euler) without smallness or near-equilibrium assumptions.
artifact.category_tag: Boltzmann equation regularity and hydrodynamic limits
artifact.status_search_result: The hydrodynamic limit toward the incompressible Navier–Stokes–Fourier system from DiPerna–Lions renormalized solutions has been rigorously established (Golse–Saint-Raymond, and extensions to bounded domains by Masmoudi–Saint-Raymond, etc.). Some velocity-regularization/compactness results exist for non-cutoff kernels (Alexandre–Desvillettes–Villani–Wennberg, and Chen–Desvillettes for long-range interactions). However, the full regularity theory for arbitrary renormalized solutions and rigorous derivation of the incompressible/compressible Euler limits in this generality remain open. Thus the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: The Navier–Stokes limit of the Boltzmann equation for bounded collision kernels
status_evidence.snippet: Renormalized solutions of the Boltzmann equation converge, as the mean free path goes to zero, to weak solutions of the incompressible Navier–Stokes equations.
status_evidence.claim: Navier–Stokes hydrodynamic limit from renormalized solutions has been rigorously derived.

status_evidence.title: Regularity of renormalized solutions in the Boltzmann equation with long-range interactions
status_evidence.snippet: Renormalized solutions enjoy some regularity/compactness in velocity when the angular kernel is nonintegrable.
status_evidence.claim: Partial regularity (velocity-direction) is known for non-cutoff kernels.

status_evidence.title: Hydrodynamic Limits (Golse, 4ECM survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Truncation and regularity issues are crucial in obtaining rigorous convergence from renormalized solutions; the Euler scaling remains problematic because entropy production does not balance streaming.
status_evidence.claim: Euler-scaling hydrodynamic limit from renormalized solutions remains open.
